pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

2. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

3. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

4. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language School.

5. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. going
   D. goed

6. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

7. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.

8. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.

9. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.

10. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Only one word repeated

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

12. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Language Welcome and and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

2. C — Where is the library?

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

5. B — went

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

10. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

11. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Attentive listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Language Welcome and; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
